Participants described organisational pressures, variability in knowledge and implementation, and limited parental involvement as factors influencing these patterns. A persistent gap between risk awareness and clinical action emerged from the interviews. Conclusion Participants suggest that vascular access care is influenced by interacting organisational, behavioural, knowledge-related, and relational factors that may reinforce reactive practice. Promoting anticipatory vascular access care through structured, workflow-integrated approaches may improve consistency, reduce avoidable harm, and support safer vascular access care. Impact Identifies a predominantly reactive pattern of vascular access care within neonatal nurses' accounts across three tertiary NICUs. Identifies organisational, behavioural, knowledge-related, and relational factors that may contribute to delayed escalation beyond technical considerations. Extends existing literature by providing insight into factors that may contribute to repeated peripheral catheter failure and delayed escalation in routine practice. Supports consideration of structured, anticipatory vascular access approaches integrated into clinical workflows to reduce avoidable harm and improve patient safety.

title: Editor’s Focus
Claudin-3 as a marker of intestinal permeability and its relation to inflammatory status in adolescents with functional gastrointestinal disorders
abstract: Abstract Background Functional Gastrointestinal disorders (FGIDs) are highly prevalent among adolescents. Increased intestinal permeability plays a potential role in the pathogenesis of FGIDs. Claudin-3 (CLDN3) may serve as an indicator of gut barrier integrity. We aimed to assess serum level of CLDN3 as a noninvasive biomarker of intestinal permeability in adolescents with FGIDs, and its relation with inflammatory markers. Methods This study included 70 adolescents with FGIDs and 65 healthy controls. Serum levels of CLDN3 and inflammatory markers; C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα), and haptoglobin, were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Results Serum levels of CLDN3 and inflammatory markers; CRP, Il-6, TNFα and haptoglobin, were significantly higher in cases compared to controls ( p = 0.02, 0.039, 0.04, 0.021 and 0.001, respectively). We detected significant positive correlations between serum level of CLDN3 and that of CRP, IL-6 and haptoglobin in cases. Conclusion Our results revealed significant elevations in serum levels of CLDN3 and inflammatory markers in adolescents with FGIDs. Significant positive correlations were detected between levels of CLDN3 and that of CRP, IL-6 and haptoglobin, suggesting an association between intestinal barrier dysfunction and low-grade systemic inflammation. Thus, CLDN3 represents a potential noninvasive biomarker of intestinal permeability in FGIDs. Impact This research investigated the potential role of Claudin-3 (CLDN3) as a noninvasive biomarker of intestinal permeability in adolescents with Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders (FGIDs), and its relation to the inflammatory status of these patients. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to assess serum CLDN3 as a noninvasive biomarker of intestinal permeability in FGIDs; previous researches have assessed intestinal barrier disruption in FGIDs based on intestinal biopsies. Our findings suggest that impaired intestinal barrier function may promote development of FGIDs by inducing inflammation. Thus, restoration of intestinal barrier integrity may represent a potential therapeutic target for FGIDs.

title: Heart rate variability after hospital discharge in perinatal risk populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Perinatal risk factors such as preterm birth, intrauterine growth restriction, and low birth weight are linked to elevated cardiovascular and neurodevelopmental risk. Heart rate variability (HRV) is widely used to assess autonomic function in these populations, yet findings remain inconsistent. While autonomic differences during the NICU period are well established, less is known about HRV after hospital discharge across childhood and adulthood. Methods PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and APA PsycArticles were searched through April 2025, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and reference screening. Peer-reviewed studies comparing HRV between perinatal risk populations and healthy full-term controls after hospital discharge were eligible. We extracted 156 effect sizes from 27 studies. Results Overall effects were modest and highly heterogeneous (d = -0.21, p = 0.14; I² = 89.3%). Growth-related conditions (small-for-gestational-age, intrauterine growth restriction) showed the most consistent HRV reductions. Preterm birth and low birth weight showed no significant overall effects but substantial between-study heterogeneity across age groups. Younger samples showed larger group differences than older samples. Conclusion Autonomic associations with perinatal risk factors appear condition-specific and age-dependent, although the predominantly cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about within-individual change. Findings underscore the importance of age- and condition-specific assessment and the need for longitudinal follow-up. Impact HRV associations with perinatal risk factors are condition-specific and vary across age. Effect sizes were most consistent for growth-related conditions (small-for-gestational-age and intrauterine growth restriction), pronounced in preterm-born infants but smaller and more variable in older groups, and small or non-significant for low and extremely low birth weight samples. This is the first meta-analysis to quantify HRV differences across perinatal risk populations from infancy to adulthood, focusing on the post-discharge period and showing that timing and etiology, rather than parameter choice, drive inconsistencies. The findings guide condition-specific assessment and underscore the need for longitudinal studies separating catch-up from survivor bias.

title: Endothelial metabolism in CDH: mitochondrial dysfunction as a new piece of the puzzle
abstract: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) remains one of the most challenging developmental lung diseases in neonatal medicine. Despite major advances in prenatal risk stratification, fetal intervention, neonatal intensive care, and extracorporeal support, pulmonary hypoplasia and pulmonary hypertension continue to determine morbidity and mortality. In this issue of Pediatric Research , Emrick and colleagues add an important dimension to the biology of CDH by showing that primary endothelial cells from affected newborns display a distinct mitochondrial phenotype characterized by metabolic activation, reduced bioenergetic efficiency, oxidative stress, and structural remodeling. 1 Their findings support a view of CDH not simply as a mechanically compressed lung, but as a developmental disorder in which intrinsic cellular abnormalities contribute to abnormal pulmonary growth and vascular adaptation.

title: Beyond ECMO: rethinking drivers of long-term outcomes in critically ill children
abstract: Pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) saves lives, but its long-term neurodevelopmental cost has been difficult to isolate from the burden of critical illness itself. Le Helleye and colleagues address this with a prospective, matched case-control study comparing ECMO survivors to general PICU survivors matched for age, diagnosis, and admission year. Overall health-related quality of life (HRQoL) was modestly lower in ECMO survivors. Physical functioning, however, showed a clear and robust deficit, persisting even against critically ill comparators. Psychosocial functioning did not differ significantly between groups, suggesting this domain is driven more by contextual and family factors than ECMO-specific injury. Roughly one-third of the entire cohort-ECMO and non-ECMO alike-showed clinically significant executive dysfunction, which proved the strongest independent predictor of poor HRQoL across all domains, outweighing ECMO's own effect. Parental stress emerged as a comparably powerful, and modifiable, mediator of child outcomes. Together these findings argue for reframing post-PICU follow-up: neurodevelopmental monitoring and structured family psychological support as core components of critical care recovery.

title: Prenatal exposure to nonpersistent endocrine disruptors and early childhood BMI: single pollutant and mixture analyses from the ECHO Program
abstract: BACKGROUND: Exposure to non-persistent endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), including phenols and phthalates, has been linked to obesity risk. While many studies focus on single-chemical exposures, mixture effects on child adiposity remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: To assess associations of prenatal phenol and phthalate exposures, singly and as mixtures, with early childhood BMI in the U.S. Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Program. METHODS: We included 586 mother-child pairs from three ECHO sites with 23 phenols and phthalate metabolites measured in maternal urine during pregnancy, and child BMI z-scores (BMIZ) at 2-5 years. Associations were estimated using covariate-adjusted single-pollutant linear regression and two mixture methods: Bayesian Weighted Quantile Sum (BWQS) and Bayesian Kernel Machine Regression (BKMR). Sex-specific effects were examined in stratified models. RESULTS: No associations were observed between the overall prenatal EDC mixture and BMIZ. In single-pollutant models, MBzP (highest tertile) was inversely associated with BMIZ (β = -0.36, 95% CI: -0.63, -0.08), while MEP (second tertile) was positively associated (β = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.01, 0.53). Among boys, MBP (second tertile) was positively associated (β = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.11, 0.79). CONCLUSIONS: We found no strong evidence for mixture effects, though some individual compounds showed non-linear and sex-specific associations. IMPACT: Using a 23-analyte panel of phenols and phthalate metabolites, and complementary (BKMR, BWQS) alongside single-pollutant and sex-stratified models, this study strengthens inference and addresses limitations of prior research. Prenatal exposure to ubiquitous, short-lived endocrine-disrupting phthalates showed non-monotonic, sex-specific associations with early childhood BMI in single-pollutant models. These findings contribute to the limited evidence base on mixture effects of endocrine-disrupting chemicals in early-life obesity risk.

title: Editing the rulebook: building the policy environment for children to access gene therapy
authors: On behalf of the Pediatric Policy Council

title: Global, regional, national trends and economic evaluation of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia burden, 2003–2023
abstract: Severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia remains a preventable cause of neonatal death and lifelong neurologic disability, yet contemporary global estimates are limited. Using Global Burden of Disease 2023 data for 204 countries, we analyzed incidence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) from extreme hyperbilirubinemia (EHB) among neonates from 2003 to 2023, applying joinpoint regression, income-stratified k-means clustering and correlation analysis, and value-per-statistical-life (VSL) and human-capital economic valuation. Globally, incident cases fell 29% (542,966-387,366) and deaths fell 66% (70,907-24,050); the mortality-to-incidence ratio halved from 13.1% to 6.2%. The average annual percent change was -1.5% for incidence and -5.0% for mortality. The Middle East and North Africa had the largest declines in cases (61%) and deaths (72%). In 2023, South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa accounted for 68% of incident cases and 90% of deaths, lower-middle-income countries for roughly two-thirds of deaths and DALYs, and India, Pakistan, and Nigeria for about half of global mortality. Incidence and mortality were strongly correlated in low-income countries (r = 0.72) but decoupled in upper-middle-income countries (r = 0.19; P = 0.167). The 2023 burden represented $6.9-10.4 billion in VSL-based welfare losses and $13.0 billion in DALY-based human-capital losses. Progress is substantial but uneven across World Bank regions and income groups. IMPACT: Severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and kernicterus remain important causes of preventable neonatal death and lifelong neurologic disability. Contemporary evidence is limited on how the burden has changed across regions and income groups and whether neonatal jaundice incidence remains closely associated with mortality. Between 2003 and 2023, modeled incident cases decreased by 29%, while deaths declined by 66%. The burden was mostly concentrated in South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and lower-middle-income countries. Incidence was strongly associated with mortality in low-income settings but largely decoupled from mortality in upper-middle-income settings. Future studies should link burden estimates with screening coverage, bilirubin measurement, phototherapy quality, referral capacity and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes to identify modifiable health-system factors and guide context-specific interventions.

title: Pediatric effects of forever chemicals may last for a long time
abstract: Abstract Perfluorinated alkylate substances (PFASs) have been in use for about 75 years. Because of their persistence, concentrations in the environment have increased, and absorbed PFAS will remain in the human body, some compounds for many years. The fetus and the newborn infant are particularly vulnerable to PFAS toxicity due to the intense development of organs and body functions. In addition, PFASs pass the placenta so that a pregnant woman shares her accumulated PFAS burden with the progeny. In addition, PFASs are excreted in the milk, so that the resulting serum-PFAS concentration in the infant may greatly exceed that of the mother. Multi-organ effects have been reported, some related to endocrine disruption. Immunotoxicity can occur at very low exposure levels, with elevated risks of infectious disease and possibly also cancer development. Unfortunately, little research was carried out during the first 50 years of industrial use, and some study reports were hidden. Independent research has been carried out only recently. Due to incomplete evidence, governmental regulations have been delayed and remain insufficient, in part because of objections from industrial interests. Impact The perfluorinated alkylate substances (PFASs) are persistent and accumulate in the environment and in the human body. The greatest risk of PFAS toxicity occurs at early age, as PFASs are transferred through the placenta and human milk. This means that early-life exposures may trigger development of diseases and other adverse outcomes that may seriously burden adult health. Research has been delayed due to secrecy. While pediatric studies in this field are underway, prudent decisions to protect public health should be made despite possible concerns regarding incomplete evidence. Practical complications, and current guidelines and interventions are by far insufficient. Current evidence on PFASs shows that these industrial chemicals are persistent and that highly elevated exposures occur already at early age. The maternal body burden of PFAS is shared with the fetus, and substantial amounts are transferred in human milk, thus impacting the unique nutritional advantage of breast-feeding. Recent evidence suggests that early PFAS exposure can affect public health, also during adult age, and that some adverse effects may be transferred to the next generation.

title: Kawasaki disease: a primer for the classification of multisystem inflammatory disorders
Beyond diagnosing acute kidney injury: defining what we need from kidney biomarkers
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critically ill children and is associated with worse short- and long-term outcomes. 1 Yet, despite considerable progress in our understanding of AKI, its diagnosis at the bedside still relies largely on serum creatinine and urine output, both of which have known drawbacks. Though, both are useful measures of kidney function, neither tells us whether there is structural kidney injury, what is driving the fall in kidney function, or how likely it is to recover. 2 For the clinician looking after a critically ill child, these are often the questions that matter most.

title: Adolescents’ and parents’ perspectives on addressing adverse childhood experiences in school-based health centers
abstract: Abstract Background School-based health centers (SBHCs) serve many children impacted by adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), but little is known about addressing ACEs in these settings. This study explored the barriers and facilitators to addressing ACEs in SBHCs from the perspectives of adolescents and parents/caregivers in the community. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with adolescents (ages 16–22) and parents/caregivers of school-aged youth (ages 3–17) recruited from patient and family advisory groups, primary care clinic waiting rooms, and snowball sampling. We used a thematic analysis approach and continued until reaching saturation. Results Twenty interviews were conducted (10 adolescents, 10 parents/caregivers). Four themes emerged, emphasizing the importance of relational context: (1) Participants expect trust between the patient and the provider addressing ACEs, (2) The school’s social environment influences comfort with addressing ACEs, (3) Relationships and contexts outside school impact perceptions of addressing ACEs, and (4) Addressing ACEs in SBHCs can promote the health of the school community. Conclusion SBHCs can play a vital role in educating about the management and impacts of ACEs. Addressing ACEs in SBHCs requires attention to the relational ecosystem. Policies and practices may consider addressing patient-provider relationships, the school environment, and broader social ecological contexts. Impact School-based health centers (SBHCs) are understudied settings that may hold promise for addressing adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). This study is the first to explore barriers and facilitators to addressing ACEs in SBHCs from the perspectives of adolescents and parents/caregivers in the community. Relational context, including the patient-provider relationship, the school’s social environment, and broader community influences, informed participants’ attitudes toward addressing ACEs in SBHCs. SBHCs have several advantages that may promote the health and well-being of youth with ACEs. These findings may inform the development of family-centered strategies to support youth with ACEs in SBHCs.

title: Inflammatory burden and coronary aneurysm risk in Kawasaki disease: appraising the Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation
abstract: Impact The Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation (AISI) may serve as an additional inflammatory marker for identifying children with Kawasaki disease (KD) who require closer coronary surveillance. AISI integrates standard hematological parameters and may complement, rather than replace, established clinical and echocardiographic risk assessment. Current evidence supports further prospective validation before AISI can be included in treatment decision pathways. AISI-based risk stratification may contribute to future personalized approaches in KD management.

title: Current perspectives and future horizons in predicting response to nutrition therapy in children with Crohn’s disease – a narrative review
abstract: Exclusive enteral nutrition (EEN) and partial enteral nutrition (PEN) alongside Crohn's Disease Exclusion Diet (CDED) are evidence-based treatment strategies for children with Crohn's disease. However, the remission rates induced through nutritional therapy vary depending on the research design, treatment population, and outcome definition. The growing body of evidence highlights the necessity of a transitioning from "one-treatment-suits-all" strategy towards "tailor-made" precision-based therapeutic approach in children with Crohn's disease to obtain the optimal treatment response. Precise personalized therapeutic plan created on the patient's treatment-responsiveness phenotype prior to the treatment initiation appears to be an utmost need for children with Crohn's disease. A personalized approach to treatment has multiple benefits for individuals and the healthcare system. The identification of reliable predictors of treatment response is crucial for selecting the optimal therapy for individuals. In this review we aim to present a state-of-the-art summary of the current knowledge on predictive factors of response to nutrition therapy defined as EEN, and PEN with CDED in children with Crohn's disease. The exploration of treatment predictors may be a small but crucial step toward individualized therapeutic approach in this group of patients, potentially enabling the selection of the most appropriate therapy for each individual patient. IMPACT: This review synthetizes the current knowledge on predictive factors of a response to nutrition therapy in children with Crohn's disease. Early clinical improvement and reduction of faecal calprotectin are potential indicators of positive outcome of nutritional therapy in Crohn's disease. The anticipation of treatment response transcends patients' stratification based on clinical characteristics assemblages. Integration of clinical and multiomic data into a decision-making approach may facilitate personalized treatment in the future. However, current literature provides insufficient evidence for definitive predictors of response to nutritional therapy in Crohn's disease.

title: The potential role of miR-34a and miR-34c in the regulation of pediatric high-grade glioma 4 aggressiveness
abstract: Abstract Background Pediatric diffuse high-grade gliomas grade 4 (pHGG-4), the most aggressive malignant primary brain tumors, are incurable and associated with poor prognosis. In most pHGG-4 , meaningful genetic aberrations were rarely found, and the aggressiveness is derived from epigenetic changes and dysregulated gene expression. miRNAs are significant epigenetic regulators of gene expression that play important roles in many cancers. Methods miR-34a and miR-34c levels were analyzed in pHGG cell lines and tumor datasets. SF188 and KNS42 cells were transfected with miR-34a/miR-34c mimic or scrambled oligonucleotide, and examined for viability, migration ability, and invasiveness. Expression of survival, cell cycle arrest/progression, apoptosis, and Epithelial–Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) regulating genes was examined using quantitative PCR (qPCR), western blot, and immunofluorescence assays. Results miR-34a and miR-34c were scarcely expressed in pHGG-4 cell lines, and miR-34c was downregulated in pHGG-4 tumor datasets. Upregulating miR-34a/miR-34c decreased cell viability, migration ability, and invasiveness, while differentially affecting the expression of genes involved in survival, cell progression, proliferation, cell cycle arrest or death, and EMT promotion, depending on the miRNA and cell line. Conclusions miR-34a and miR-34c are multifunctional tumor suppressors that play an important regulatory role in pHGG-4 aggressiveness. Both miRNAs can serve as excellent and powerful therapeutic tools against pHGG-4 . Impact This study revealed miR-34a and miR-34c as multifunctional suppressors of pHGG-4 tumor aggressiveness, both downregulated in disease models. miR-34a/miR-34c restoration decreased cell viability, migration ability, invasiveness, and stemness marker expression Both miRNAs exerted similar phenotypic effects while differentially regulated gene expression in a miRNA-associated and cell line-dependent manner The findings reinforced that epigenetic dysregulation, rather than recurrent genetic alterations, is a central driver of pHGG-4 aggressiveness. This work suggests the rational for potential miR-34-based therapeutic strategies in this otherwise incurable disease.

title: Adequate nutrition during pregnancy including LCPUFAs: a commentary
Association between eye-tracking measures and Griffiths-III developmental scores at 18 months in healthy term-born children
abstract: Background Current neurodevelopmental assessment tools strive to identify atypical development but have limitations. This study explored the potential of eye-tracking (ET) as an objective tool for assessing neurodevelopment at 18 months of age. Methods Healthy term-born children were prospectively recruited. At 18 months of age, participants underwent ET assessment and developmental assessment using the Griffiths Scales of Child Development-3rd edition (Griffiths-III). ET tasks assessed working memory, visual attention, and social cognition. Measures extracted from the ET tasks included first fixation, mean fixation duration, and saccadic reaction time. Pearson's correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression analyses were used to examine associations between ET measures and Griffiths-III scores and subscales. Results Fifty-three children were included. The ET happy task (measures social cognition) showed the strongest correlation with Griffiths-III scales; mean fixation duration on the mouth was significantly associated with subscale A (Foundations of Learning) (r = 0.30, p = 0.03), subscale B (Language and Communication) (r = 0.57, p Conclusion Eye-tracking measures, especially those measuring social cognition (Happy task) were associated with early language, social-emotional, and general developmental outcomes at 18 months of age. These findings support further investigation of ET as a complimentary objective approach for early neurodevelopmental assessment. Impact Eye-tracking (ET) measures were associated with four of the five Griffiths-III subscales and overall General Development (GD) in a cohort of healthy term-born children. The strongest associations were observed between measures in the happy task and the Language and Communication subscale (Griffiths-III, subscale B). ET may provide complementary markers of early language, social cognition, and general developmental outcomes. Multivariable models combining ET measures explained variance in Griffiths-III outcomes, particularly in the Foundations of Learning, Language and Communication, and Personal-Social-Emotional subscales. Future research should focus on developing age-appropriate ET tasks with standardized scoring for the early assessment of language, communication, and social development.

title: Non-medical drivers of health and pediatric no-show prediction: identifying modifiable risk factors
abstract: Abstract Background No-shows to medical appointments contribute to disruptions and inefficiencies in healthcare delivery. While artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) models are increasingly used to predict no-shows, few have incorporated non-medical drivers of health (NMDOH), particularly in pediatric populations. This study evaluated the inclusion of NMDOH in pediatric AI/ML no-show prediction and identified modifiable factors associated with no-shows. Methods A retrospective study was conducted of scheduled pediatric appointments across six general pediatrics clinics during April–August 2024 using electronic health record and NMDOH screening data. A transformer-based AI/ML no-show model was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with no-show status. Results Among 7,931 included appointments, 2761 (34.8%) were no-shows. Models with and without NMDOH variables showed similar performance (AUROC 0.708 for both; AUPRC 0.536 vs. 0.535, respectively). Inclusion of patient demographic and insurance variables produced a small improvement in performance, with similar results with and without NMDOH inclusion (AUROC 0.721 and AUPRC 0.542 for both). No-shows were associated with unconfirmed appointments, non-active patient portal status, transportation needs, and housing instability. Conclusions NMDOH variables did not significantly change model performance but identified actionable factors associated with no-shows. Prediction models may be most useful when paired with targeted outreach and barrier-reduction strategies. Impact Non-medical drivers of health (NMDOH), including transportation needs and housing instability, as well as appointment confirmation and patient portal activation, were associated with missed pediatric appointments. Inclusion of NMDOH in AI/ML no-show prediction models did not meaningfully change prediction performance. The associations highlight modifiable barriers that can be targeted through clinical and operational interventions. AI-based no-show prediction may be most effective when paired with outreach and barrier-reduction strategies.

title: Management of Peripheral Venous Access Devices (PVADs): Neonatal European Vascular Access Team - ESPR recommendation 5
authors: on behalf of the Pediatric and Neonatal Vascular Access Special Interest Group (SIG) of the European Society for Pediatric Research (ESPR) and Neonatal European Vascular Access Team (NEVAT)
abstract: Impact Vascular access is a pervasive facet of contemporary neonatal practice, yet it lacks standardization, and some practices lack supporting evidence. This recommendation introduces a structured, evidence-based approach to neonatal peripheral venous access, addressing longstanding challenges such as high failure rates and inconsistent clinical practices. Its novelty lies in integrating advanced visualization tools, standardized assessment protocols (RaSuVA, TLC), and modern securement strategies to optimize catheter longevity and safety. By shifting from habit-driven decisions to individualized vascular access planning, it sets a new standard for safer, more effective neonatal IV therapy.

title: Analysis of brain iron deposition in an in vivo model of pediatric autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
abstract: Abstract Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) represents one form of chronic kidney disease (CKD) affecting the pediatric population. CKD in early life has been associated with neurocognitive deficits and disturbances in iron metabolism. Excess iron accumulation may exacerbate inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways linked to neurocognitive decline in CKD. No animal studies have yet investigated brain iron metabolism in early-life CKD, including PKD, or confirmed these findings through histological analysis. Utilizing a conditional Pkd2 knockout mouse, we investigated the effect of kidney disease on early brain development and brain iron deposition through neuroimaging and histology. By postnatal day 19, PKD mice had significantly increased blood urea nitrogen (BUN, mean = 141 mg/dL ± 0.6, p < 0.01) and cyst burden (mean = 83.1% ± 5.4, p < 0.01). Brain volumetrics did not differ longitudinally between groups; however, PKD mice had significantly shorter T2* relaxation times across multiple brain regions (total brain, gray and white matter, cerebral cortex, cerebellum, brainstem, hippocampus, and globus pallidus), indicating increased iron deposition. Perl’s Prussian blue staining confirmed increased iron in the cerebral cortex of PKD mice. These findings extend prior human CKD neuroimaging data and provide a platform to investigate mechanisms of iron-mediated neuroinjury in early-life CKD

title: Community-based monitoring of neonatal jaundice using the point-of-care Bilistick® System 2.0
authors: the neonatologists and nurses of the Rooming in Unit
responsible for staff training and technical supervision for Bilimetrix
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neonatal jaundice often peaks after discharge, creating the need for reliable post-discharge monitoring. This study evaluated the feasibility and safety of a hospital-to-community pathway using the Bilistick® System 2.0 within routine Community Health Family Services (CHFS). METHODS: This retrospective observational study was conducted within a Local Health Authority in northeastern Italy. Newborns eligible for out-of-hospital bilirubin testing according to a Diagnostic-Therapeutic Assistance Pathway (DTAP) were referred either to CHFS or to hospital follow-up based on bilirubin risk profile, clinical factors, and organizational considerations. RESULTS: Of 397 eligible newborns meeting inclusion criteria, 244 were included. Of these, 108 (44.3%) were referred to CHFS, 135 (55.3%) to hospital follow-up, and 1 was lost to follow-up. Among newborns referred to CHFS, 97 (89.8%) completed monitoring without hospital referral. Eleven were referred to the hospital, of whom 7 received phototherapy. Among newborns referred directly to the hospital, 6 (4.4%) required phototherapy. No sampling-related adverse events, missed phototherapy, exchange transfusions, or cases of kernicterus were recorded. CONCLUSION: Community-based bilirubin monitoring using the Bilistick® System 2.0 appears feasible and safe for selected low-risk newborns within a structured hospital-to-community pathway. IMPACT: To our knowledge, this is the first real-world evaluation of a structured hospital-to-community pathway integrating point-of-care bilirubin testing into routine community care within UNICEF's Baby-Friendly Initiative framework. Among selected newborns referred to community services, 89.8% completed bilirubin monitoring without hospital referral. Community midwives identified infants requiring escalation of care; no missed phototherapy, exchange transfusion, or kernicterus occurred. The model may reduce unnecessary hospital reassessment and disruption to the mother-infant dyad; local administrative estimates indicate a direct cost difference of €32.30 per bilirubin reassessment.

title: Targeted proteomics in late-onset neonatal sepsis: an exploratory analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Late-onset neonatal sepsis (LONS) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in preterm infants, but early diagnosis remains difficult. We aimed to identify candidate proteomic biomarkers of LONS and evaluate whether these changes could be reproduced by in vitro stimulation. METHODS: Longitudinal blood samples were collected from preterm neonates with suspected LONS and non-septic controls in two neonatal intensive care units, at onset and after 24 and 48 hours. In parallel, whole blood from preterm neonates without LONS was stimulated in vitro with E. coli and S. epidermidis. Protein expression was quantified using targeted proteomics. RESULTS: Fifteen neonates with LONS, eight controls, and ten in vitro stimulation samples were included. Sixty-six proteins showed altered expression during LONS. Upregulated proteins were predominantly cytokines and chemokines, whereas downregulated proteins were associated with development, growth, and metabolism. Most alterations normalized within 48 hours. In vitro stimulation reproduced expression changes for a subset of proteins, suggesting direct pathogen-induced immune responses. CONCLUSION: LONS in preterm neonates is associated with dynamic proteomic alterations. Combined clinical and in vitro analyses identified biologically relevant candidate biomarkers that may support future diagnostic and monitoring strategies. Further validation in larger, independent cohorts is required before clinical use. IMPACT: Late-onset neonatal sepsis in preterm neonates is associated with pronounced and dynamic changes in protein expression patterns. Targeted proteomics identified candidate biomarkers related to inflammatory signaling, growth, and metabolic pathways. Longitudinal analyses demonstrated rapid normalization of many proteins within 48 hours after sepsis onset. In vitro stimulation distinguished proteins directly induced by pathogen exposure from secondary systemic responses. The identified proteins may serve as targets for future research into diagnostic and monitoring biomarkers for neonatal sepsis in preterm infants.

title: Management of umbilical venous and arterial catheter: Neonatal European Vascular Access Team- ESPR Recommendation 2
authors: on behalf of the Pediatric and Neonatal Vascular Access SIG of the ESPR and NEVAT
abstract: Impact The importance of standardized protocols for assessment, insertion and evaluation is highlighted. Implementation of this recommendation improves patient safety and reduces practice variation.

title: Advancing prenatal metal research in birth size using mixture approaches
Pro-inflammatory and matricellular protein expression patterns associated with bronchopulmonary dysplasia severity
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary inflammation and dysregulated repair have been linked to the development of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), but disease severity varies widely, and the mechanisms leading to BPD heterogeneity remain unclear. We hypothesized that levels of pro-inflammatory and matricellular proteins in preterm infants airways in the first week of life are associated with BPD severity. Methods We collected tracheal aspirates from preterm infants, born ≤32 weeks gestational age, receiving mechanical ventilation in the first week of life. Protein levels were measured in the supernatants. BPD severity categories were defined by the Jensen classification. Results We observed three distinct expression patterns, including (i) proteins increased in any BPD severity, most significantly pro-inflammatory interleukin (IL)-17A and IL-23, (ii) proteins elevated only in grade 1 BPD (IL-12 isoforms, the matricellular protein periostin), and (iii) proteins decreased in grade 2/3 BPD, notably the matricellular protein thrombospondin 1 (THBS1). Low THBS1 discriminated grade 2/3 BPD, whereas high periostin levels discriminated grade 1 BPD, adjusting for sex and birth weight. Conclusions Tracheal aspirate levels of select pro-inflammatory and matricellular proteins show distinct patterns associated with BPD severity categories. THBS1 and periostin, tissue repair, immune, and angiogenesis regulators, display differential expression and potential roles as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in the pathogenesis of BPD severity categories. Impact We identify differential patterns and relationships between pro-inflammatory cytokine and matricellular protein expression levels in preterm infant airways by bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) severity. Particularly, low levels of the matricellular protein thrombospondin 1 discriminated grade 2/3 BPD from grade 1 and 0, whereas high levels of the matricellular protein periostin discriminated grade 1 BPD, all after adjusting for sex and birth weight. Quantifying pro-inflammatory and tissue repair signals in preterm infant airways provides novel insights into early mechanisms that may impact BPD severity. Early biomarkers of BPD severity can provide crucial information for diagnosis, prognosis, and potential future treatment selection.

title: Ensemble model–based prediction of school–age asthma risk in children with food allergy
abstract: Background Early-life food allergy (FA) is a major childhood asthma risk, but prospective screening tools for high-risk infants aged 0-2 are lacking, delaying early intervention. Objective To develop an ensemble-learning model with cost-sensitive optimization for early asthma risk screening in FA infants (0-2 years) and provide quantitative clinical decision support. Methods This prospective cohort enrolled 447 FA-confirmed infants (0-2 years), collecting 135 baseline predictors across 7 categories. After median 4.5-year follow-up to school age (≥6 years), we generated 3 clinically interpretable features and built a two-stage weighted ensemble (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Residual Networks) with cost-sensitive learning (missed-to-false-alarm ratio = 5:1) to optimize thresholds. Results On the independent test set, AUC = 0.886, recall = 1.00 (zero missed). Decision-curve analysis showed superior net benefit across broad thresholds, including optimal cutoff 0.09. Top predictors: RSV infection, wheeze frequency, nocturnal sleep, antibiotic exposure, and rhinitis duration. Sensitivity analysis confirmed stable zero missed at cost ratios ≥5:1, indicating 5:1 was not the key driver. Conclusion The model preliminarily predicts school-age asthma risk in FA infants. Its high-recall design avoids missed diagnoses and offers quantitative references for early intervention and individualized follow-up before age 2. Impact Core finding: A performance-weighted ensemble model predicts school-age asthma in food-allergic infants (0-2 years) with an AUC of 0.886 and recall 1.00 using only clinical data. Contribution: A cost-sensitive, feature-engineered model tailored to this high-risk population; identifies RSV, wheeze grading, and antibiotic load as top predictors. Significance Enables early, non-invasive screening before age 2, avoids missed high-risk children, and supports targeted preventive interventions in primary care.

title: Impact on mortality of inhaled nitric oxide in newborns ≤34 weeks with early hypoxemic respiratory failure: systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Introduction Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is approved for hypoxemic respiratory failure (HRF) associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH) in term and near-term neonates; however, its use in preterm infants ≤34 weeks' gestation remains controversial, with limited and inconsistent evidence of survival benefit. Objective To evaluate the association between iNO use and mortality in preterm neonates ≤34 weeks' gestation. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Major databases were searched up to October 11, 2025. Observational studies and clinical trials reporting mortality in preterm infants with early HRF treated with iNO were included. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed. Results Nineteen studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and six (n = 556 infants) in the meta-analysis. Study quality ranged from poor to good, with limitations related to confounding and heterogeneity. No significant reduction in mortality was observed with iNO compared with standard care (RR 0.65; 95% CI 0.29-1.48; I² = 55.7%). Infants receiving iNO were more severely ill at baseline. A positive oxygenation response was associated with improved outcomes and varied by gestational age (GA), timing of PH onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and hypoxemia severity. Conclusions Current evidence regarding the survival benefit of iNO in preterm infants ≤34 weeks remains inconclusive. Impact This systematic review and meta-analysis show that inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is not associated with a consistent reduction in mortality in preterm infants ≤34 weeks at the population level. It adds evidence that outcomes are strongly influenced by clinical context, particularly, illness severity, gestational age, timing of pulmonary hypertension onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and response to therapy. These findings support a selective, phenotype-driven approach rather than routine iNO use in all preterm infants with hypoxemic respiratory failure. The results may inform clinical decision-making and highlight the need for well-designed randomized trials in this high-risk population.

title: Infant microbiome development: a renewed focus on the second six months and complementary feeding
abstract: The infant microbiome is increasingly recognised as an important factor in human health and disease. It plays a fundamental role in the development of the immune system, and early life dysbiosis is associated with a wide variety of diseases in later life, including asthma, allergy, diabetes and auto-immune diseases. 1

title: Family reflections: the questions we learn to ask
Strategies to increase participant diversity in pediatric research: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Background Multiple strategies have been introduced to improve research recruitment and retention of underserved children and young people (CYP) with long-term conditions. For the first time, this systematic review presents a structured description of CYP and caregiver preferences for these strategies and collates evidence of their impact on participation. Methods The Embase, MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL databases were searched. Studies were included from the inception of the database to September 2025 if they were undertaken in a high-income country, with CYP under 19 years with a long-term condition. Results We assessed 16,727 records and included 21 studies published between 1998 and 2024, all based in the USA, predominantly drawn from African American and Latino populations. We determined preferences for the positive impact of the use of familiar venues and culturally attuned community events for study activities; communication that was bilingual, used educational games or social media; reliable and equitable relationships with study facilitators; and the co-production of recruitment strategies and study interventions. Conclusions There was a lack of comparative evidence across individual approaches. The time and resources needed to build awareness, trust, and facilitate research participation in underserved CYP need broader acknowledgement from funders and policymakers. Impact The review highlights how building trust, maintaining contact, and using familiar language and venues for study activities can improve research recruitment and retention in under-researched children and young people. The additional time and resources required to increase the diversity of children and young people participating in research need to be understood by funding bodies. The review’s structured description of recruitment and retention strategies and their comparative effectiveness provides valuable and practical insight for those wishing to diversify research participation.

title: Motor-cognitive integrated training improves executive function and gross motor skills in children with developmental coordination disorder: a pilot RCT
abstract: Background To evaluate a school-based pilot intervention combining fundamental movement skills (FMS) training and action observation and motor imagery (AOMI) for gross motor skills and executive function in developmental coordination disorder (DCD). Methods In this pilot randomized controlled trial, 20 children with DCD were randomized to an experimental group (FMS plus AOMI, n = 10) or an active control group (FMS plus video-based physical activity education). Both groups completed sessions three times per week for 10 weeks. Gross motor skills were assessed using the Test of Gross Motor Development-3. Executive function was evaluated using the More-Odd Shifting, Stroop, and Spatial Working Memory tasks. Results Motor skills improved in both groups, with larger gains observed in the experimental group. For executive function, the experimental group showed greater improvements mainly in reaction time and inverse efficiency scores, whereas accuracy improvements were limited and significant only in selected conditions. Conclusion Compared with FMS combined with video-based physical activity education, FMS combined with AOMI may be associated with additional improvements in motor skills and executive function-related behavioural performance in children with DCD. Given the small pilot sample, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary rather than definitive evidence of efficacy or superiority. Clinical trial registration Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07486856. Impact Children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) commonly present with both motor coordination deficits and executive function difficulties. Existing interventions mainly focus on motor skills, whereas motor-cognitive integrated approaches remain insufficiently tested in school settings. This pilot randomized controlled trial provides preliminary evidence that a school-based programme combining fundamental movement skills training with action observation and motor imagery may be associated with larger improvements than an attention-matched active control condition involving fundamental movement skills training and video-based physical activity education.

title: Sociodemographic differences in time-specific smartphone use among a national sample of adolescents
abstract: Screen use among U.S. adolescents is ubiquitous. There is a lack of information on sociodemographic differences in time-specific usage patterns using objective measures of screen use. We examined sociodemographic differences in objectively measured time-specific smartphone use among a national, diverse sample of 233 U.S. adolescents (13-18 y; M ± SD = 15.9 ± 1.3; 46% female, 6% other gender). Participants self-reported sociodemographic characteristics, then installed a passive sensing meter on their smartphones for ≥3 days to monitor smartphone activity, including application use, duration, and timing. Multiple linear regression examined differences in smartphone usage patterns by sociodemographic factors. In fully adjusted analyses, teens who were LGBTQIA+ versus non-LGBTQIA+ (24 hr use: +0.94 h/day; evening use, 20:00-22:59: +0.22 h/evening; nighttime use, 23:00-5:59: +0.39 h/night), with less parental education (nighttime use: +0.37 h/night), and with no parental screen use limits (24 hr use: +1.24 h/day; evening use: +0.24 h/evening; nighttime use: +0.34 h/night) had greater smartphone use. This national study demonstrated that LGBTQIA+ adolescents and those with lower parental education may be at heightened risk for excessive screen use with possible impacts on wellbeing. Parental restrictions on screen use are potentially modifiable markers of youth smartphone use. IMPACT: The present study examined levels of objectively measured smartphone use among a national, diverse sample of adolescents. Our findings have broad public health implications for American adolescents. We demonstrated that adolescents who were LGBTQIA+ and those with lower parental education had higher levels of smartphone use, with potential for both beneficial and harmful impacts on health and well-being. Moreover, parental restrictions on screen use are important potential targets to help reduce smartphone use among U.S. youth.

title: Gut microbiota are linked to gastrointestinal symptoms and behavioral changes but not inflammation in autism spectrum disorder: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are increased in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We examined the relationship between ASD severity, intestinal inflammation, gut permeability, and dysbiosis. METHODS: Our cross-sectional study examined baseline data from a clinical trial and included stools from typically developing (TD) controls and siblings. GI symptom severity was assessed using GI severity index (GSI) with Bristol stool scoring, while ASD symptoms were quantified using Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2). Biomarkers including plasma zonulin, occludin, and S100A9, and fecal calprotectin levels, were measured to assess intestinal permeability and inflammation. Fecal microbiota was analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing. RESULTS: Seventy-two children with ASD were included for biomarker analysis, and 135 children's stools for microbiome analysis. A statistically significant correlation was observed between GSI and SRS-2 scores (p = 0.02). GSI and SRS-2 scores did not correlate with measured biomarkers, none of which were elevated above published normal values. Children with ASD had reduced fecal richness and distinct clustering of organisms, with increased relative abundance of Fusicatenibacter, Blautia, Sarcina, and Eubacterium, compared to TD children. CONCLUSIONS: Children with ASD who had GI symptoms had increased Bacteroides and Ruminococci. Dysbiosis correlated with common GI symptoms, including flatulence, foul stools, and nighttime awakening. IMPACT: Children with ASD who have more disturbed social awareness are prone to more severe GI symptoms, reduced fecal microbial diversity and abnormal fecal microbial composition. Certain stool microbial taxa correlated with total GI symptom scores as well as with specific GI symptoms including flatulence, abdominal pain/irritability, and foul-smelling stools. However, we found no evidence of gastrointestinal or systemic inflammation, nor of increased gut permeability to explain the symptoms.

title: Sibling factors associated with gut microbiota and fecal short-chain fatty acids in preschoolers
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sibling factors are linked not only to disease development but also to gut environmental factors (e.g., microbiota, short-chain fatty acids [SCFA]). However, these associations among preschoolers and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: In a sub-cohort study of a nationwide birth-cohort study, using fecal microbiome and SCFA data from 903 children at age 2 or 4 years, we examined associations of sibling factors with gut environmental factors. We also determined enterotypes by clustering and sibling-enterotype associations with potential mediation pathways. RESULTS: Among sibling factors, the number of older siblings showed the strongest associations with gut environmental factors. We identified 3 enterotypes: 1) Mediterraneibacter gnavus group, 2) Faecalibacterium, and 3) Ruminococcus. Compared to enterotype 2, having older siblings was associated with lower odds of enterotype 1, with the lowest Shannon index and propionate level, at age 2 (1 sibling: adjOR 0.49, 95%CI 0.34-0.69; ≥2: adjOR 0.32, 95%CI, 0.19-0.54) and 4 (1 sibling: adjOR 0.45, 95%CI 0.26-0.77; ≥2: adjOR 0.22, 95%CI 0.08-0.53) years. These associations were largely direct, with modest mediation by antibiotic use at age 4 years (1 sibling, adjOR 0.89; 95%CI, 0.79-1.00). CONCLUSION: Our data identified distinct enterotypes of preschoolers and sibling-enterotype association pathways. IMPACT: In this nationwide multicenter birth-cohort sub-cohort, older siblings were strongly associated with gut microbial composition in preschoolers. Having older siblings was associated with lower odds of a potentially less mature enterotype characterized by the lowest Shannon index and propionate level. The sibling-enterotype association was mainly direct, with modest mediation by recent antibiotic use. This study extends sibling-microbiota evidence beyond infancy/toddlerhood by identifying three enterotypes with distinct microbial and short-chain fatty acid profiles. These findings clarify pathways linking family structure to gut environmental development and may inform microbiota-targeted disease prevention strategies.

title: Trust but verify…the importance of multimethod and biomarker assessments of prenatal substance exposures
abstract: The paper by Micalizzi et al., “Insights into the validity of concurrent and retrospective maternal report of infant smoke exposure using biomarker-based validation,” is a timely reminder of the complexities of reliably assessing children’s exposure to tobacco in order to determine developmental sequelae and inform public health warnings and responses.The study capitalizes on a unique longitudinal data set derived from two sources over a 17-year period. The study found systematic bias in mothers’ recall of infant exposure, depending on whether they acknowledged or denied it. The findings highlight the need for prospective and bioverified studies of children’s exposure to ETS as well as to other substances that may harm children’s development, particularly where stigma and social undesirability, as well as degradation of memory, may influence maternal reporting. Methodological issues in developmental neurotoxicology studies are considered, including confounding factors of polysubstance use, environmental chemicals, biomarker characteristics, socioeconomic status and assessment timing, frequency and amount. Implications of the present study are important for several clinical and methodological reasons. Both biomarkers and survey reports or interview assessments are critical to increasing the accuracy of understanding the occurrence of and the thresholds for prenatal and postnatal impacts of substances such as ETS.

title: PFAS exposure in 12-year-old children and its association with metabolic markers
abstract: BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are long-lasting industrial chemicals with widespread exposure, but their effects on adolescent cardiometabolic health remain underexplored. This cross-sectional study evaluated associations between PFAS concentrations and metabolic biomarkers at age 12. METHODS: The study included 451 participants from the French PELAGIE mother-child cohort. At age 12, serum levels of six PFAS and metabolic biomarkers (leptin, adiponectin, fructosamine, total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides) were measured. Cross-sectional associations were assessed using multivariable linear regression models and Quantile G-computation mixture models, adjusted for potential confounders and stratified by sex and pubertal stage. RESULTS: In the overall population, perfluoroundecanoic acid (PFUdA) was associated with higher total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol levels. In pre-menarcheal girls, perfluorohexane sulfonate (PFHxS) was associated with higher total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol levels, and PFAS mixture analyses also showed positive associations with these lipid markers. In boys, perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) and perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) were associated with higher triglyceride levels in peripubertal boys, whereas perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) was associated with lower triglyceride levels in postpubertal boys. CONCLUSION: Findings indicate potential associations between PFAS exposure and metabolic biomarkers at age 12, with variations by sex and pubertal status, emphasizing the need for longitudinal investigations. IMPACT: PFAS were detected in all serum samples, showing widespread exposure among the adolescents. Exposure to PFAS was associated with blood lipid markers at age 12, with differences in associations observed across sex- and pubertal stage-specific groups. This study is one of the few to consider the stage of pubertal development in the associations between PFAS and metabolic health markers. The findings suggest that pubertal development should be considered when evaluating the health effects of PFAS exposure during adolescence.

title: Japan at the limits of viability: national experience and evolving outcomes of infants born at 22–23 weeks’ gestation
abstract: Infants born at 22-23 weeks' gestation represent the limits of viability with substantial international variation in outcomes. Japan has consistently reported some of the highest survival rates; however, the underlying healthcare systems and clinical practices have not been comprehensively synthesized. This review summarizes Japan's national experience using data from a nationwide network database, epidemiologic studies, clinical practice surveys, and international comparisons. Survival at discharge is approximately 60% and 80% for infants born at 22 and 23 weeks' gestation, respectively, with relatively low rates of severe intraventricular hemorrhage and necrotizing enterocolitis. Key healthcare system features include regionalized perinatal care promoting antenatal maternal transfer, a nationwide clinical network for benchmarking, and universal health insurance. Clinical practice is characterized by active resuscitation and meticulous, individualized, pathophysiology-based management, including invasive respiratory support, echocardiography-guided hemodynamic management, intensive neuroprotection, and specialized nursing care. The effectiveness of these practices remains uncertain, and further research is needed. Continuous outcome monitoring and quality improvement are essential to refine context-specific strategies. IMPACT: This review provides the comprehensive synthesis of Japan's national experience in the care of infants born at 22-23 weeks' gestation, integrating outcomes with healthcare system structures and clinical practices. It identifies key system-level and clinical factors-such as regionalized perinatal care, nationwide data-driven quality improvement, and pathophysiology-based management-that may contribute to Japan's high survival rates and relatively low morbidity. It highlights the importance of integrated "package-of-care" approaches and continuous outcome monitoring, offering insights that may inform strategies to improve outcomes at the limits of viability globally.

title: Emerging data of use of biologics in eosinophilic esophagitis in children
Neurobehavioural outcomes after term IUGR from adolescence to adulthood: a cross-species scoping review
abstract: Abstract Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) is associated with long-term neurobehavioural alterations. This scoping review mapped evidence on neurobehavioural outcomes following IUGR in term-born humans and preclinical animal models. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, six databases were searched from January 1985 to February 2025. Clinical studies were included if they assessed motor, cognitive, or anxiety outcomes in adolescents or young adults born at term with IUGR, small for gestational age (SGA), or low birth weight (LBW). Preclinical studies were included if IUGR was induced via placental insufficiency and behavioural outcomes evaluated at equivalent developmental stages. Data were charted and synthesised narratively. Twenty-eight studies (16 clinical, 12 preclinical) were included. Motor and cognitive outcomes were frequently assessed; anxiety-related behaviours were examined in fewer clinical studies despite frequent assessment in preclinical models. Motor coordination and memory outcomes were reported in both human and animal studies, though inconsistent diagnostic criteria and heterogeneous outcome measures limited cross-species comparisons. Most clinical studies classified participants as SGA or LBW; only two applied antenatal criteria to confirm IUGR. This evidence map reveals broad coverage of motor and cognitive domains but limited examination of anxiety outcomes in clinical populations. Standardising diagnostics and aligning behavioural assessments across species are priorities for translational comparability. This review was originally registered in PROSPERO (CRD42020197400) as a systematic review. The protocol has since been adapted to a scoping review framework; the PROSPERO registration reflects the original systematic review methodology, as PROSPERO does not accept scoping review registration. The adapted methodology is described in the Methods section below. Available from: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42020197400 . Impact This is the first scoping review to map both clinical and preclinical evidence on neurobehavioural outcomes following IUGR beyond childhood into adolescence and young adulthood. Motor and cognitive outcomes are widely studied across species, but anxiety domains remain under-examined, particularly in human cohorts. Diagnostic inconsistency (SGA/LBW used as proxies for IUGR) and narrow species representation in preclinical studies are major barriers to translational alignment.

title: Editor’s Focus
Clesrovimab in the new era of RSV prevention: one season, one dose, one chance
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization in infancy worldwide. Historically, prevention relied on monthly palivizumab administration for selected high-risk infants, despite evidence that a substantial proportion of severe RSV disease occurs in previously healthy term infants. The recent introduction of maternal RSV vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies has transformed the prevention landscape. Clesrovimab (MK-1654; Enflonsia) is a long-acting monoclonal antibody designed to provide season-long protection following a single dose. In the pivotal phase 2b/3 CLEVER trial, clesrovimab reduced RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization among infants entering their first RSV season, with a safety profile comparable to placebo. The absolute risk reduction for RSV hospitalization was approximately 1.9 percentage points, corresponding to an estimated number needed to treat of 51 infants over 150 days of follow-up. In this policy-focused clinical perspective informed by a narrative review, we examine the emerging role of clesrovimab within contemporary RSV prevention strategies. We discuss efficacy, safety, implementation challenges, economic considerations, and remaining evidence gaps, including the absence of head-to-head comparisons with nirsevimab, limited post-licensure data, and uncertainties regarding long-term effectiveness and affordability. Future success will depend not only on efficacy but also on equitable access, sustainable implementation, and ongoing surveillance. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The emergence of long-acting monoclonal antibodies has expanded preventive options for infants at risk of RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease during their first RSV season. For clinicians, the key shift is that RSV prevention is increasingly being considered within a broader population-health framework rather than solely as a risk-based intervention for selected high-risk groups. Clesrovimab, alongside nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination, represents one component of an evolving prevention strategy aimed at reducing RSV-associated morbidity and hospitalization during early infancy. From a practical perspective, successful implementation will depend on timely administration, integration into neonatal discharge planning and well-child care pathways, and coordination with maternal immunization programs. As RSV prevention moves into routine clinical practice, equitable access, sustained coverage, affordability, and ongoing post-licensure surveillance will be as important as efficacy demonstrated in clinical trials. Ultimately, the greatest reductions in RSV-related hospitalization are likely to result from effective delivery of preventive strategies to the infants at highest risk during the RSV season. KEY POINTS: RSV continues to impose a substantial burden on infants worldwide despite decades of clinical recognition and supportive care. Most RSV hospitalizations occur in infants without traditional high-risk conditions, highlighting the limitations of selective prophylaxis strategies. Long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSV vaccination have transformed prevention from a niche intervention into a population-level public health strategy. Clesrovimab demonstrated significant protection against RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory tract infection and hospitalization in healthy infants entering their first RSV season. Future research should focus on comparative effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, long-term safety, implementation in low-resource settings, and optimization of delivery strategies to maximize population impact.

title: Profile of human milk oligosaccharides and maternal FUT2 polymorphism: genotype-phenotype correlation and proposed cut-off for secretor status
abstract: Background Human milk oligosaccharides (HMO) are complex carbohydrates which is undigestible to humans and confer health benefits. The synthesis of HMOs is determined by fucosyltransferase enzymes, which are encoded by FUT2/FUT3 genes. Polymorphisms of the FUT2 result in various secretor status. This study aimed to identify the proportion of secretor and FUT2 genotype-phenotype correlation in Indonesian mothers. Methods This was a cross-sectional study, recruiting 120 healthy mothers aged at least 18 years who exclusively breastfed. Breastmilk samples were obtained at infant's age 2-5 weeks old. Analysis of HMO was performed using Ultra High-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Fluorescence Detection. Sequencing of entire coding region was performed to find genetic variants of FUT2. The ROC analysis was done to determine the threshold value of 2'FL based on FUT2 genotype. Results The proportion of secretor was 65.8%. A novel FUT2 variant was identified, c.851C>G. There was a significant association between secretor genotype and phenotype (p Conclusion Proportion of secretor in Indonesian is lower than of Caucasian. The widely used 2'FL cut-off at 25-50 mg/L needs to be re-evaluated based on clinical health impact or genotype findings. Impact This study answered the question of secretor proportion in Indonesian mothers (65.8%). The significant differences among countries implied that the consequences of secretor status to infant's health should be elaborated, including the contribution of less common HMOs. We demonstrated a strong correlation between FUT2 genotype-phenotype and discovered a novel FUT2 variant, c.851C>G. This study obtained a secretor cut-off at 2'FL 425 mg/L based on ROC curve for FUT2 genotype and 2'FL values. This cut-off needs to be evaluated in light of clinical impact, ideally in a longitudinal study design to capture dynamic of human milk across lactation period.

title: Higher risk of testicular atrophy after partial orchiectomy performed before one year of age
Performance of large language models in pediatric infectious disease education: a multi-condition comparative study
abstract: Abstract Background Evaluating how appropriate current large language models (LLMs) respond to common pediatric infectious disease (PID) questions is important for understanding their potential role in education and clinical support. Therefore, we evaluated and compared the clinical quality of answers produced by different LLMs when given professionally written, clinician-style case descriptions, using a purpose-built multi-domain evaluation tool. Methods Three different LLMs, including DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, ChatGPT-5, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, were investigated using 12 relevant PID scenarios. Each scenario included five open-ended questions: etiology, clinical features, diagnostics, treatment options, and complications. Two PID specialists independently reviewed all responses using a Likert scoring tool. Results All three models received high overall scores. ChatGPT-5 achieved perfect domain scores (10.0), whereas DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp showed similarly strong results, with only minor reductions in diagnostics (9.83) and treatment (9.92). Gemini 2.5 Flash demonstrated higher variability, particularly in treatment (8.83) and diagnostics (9.75), while matching the other models in clinical findings and complications (10.0) and scoring 9.83 in etiology. However, there were no statistically significant differences across models in domain-level comparisons (all p > 0.05). In addition, model-level analyses similarly demonstrated high accuracy (6.0; 5.98; 5.85), completeness (3.0; 2.97; 2.87), and safety (1.0; 1.0; 0.97) for ChatGPT-5, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, and Gemini 2.5 Flash, respectively (accuracy: p = 0.074; completeness: p = 0.066; safety: p = 0.14). Conclusion Current LLMs performed highly in structured, expert-reviewed PID scenarios and may assist with information organization and early-stage clinical reasoning. However, their optimal use remains within clinician-supervised workflows, where AI-generated outputs complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgment. Impact Current large language models (LLMs) show consistently high-quality performance across pediatric infectious disease scenarios, with no significant differences between models. Our study adds a structured, multi-domain comparison using clinician-style cases and expert evaluation, providing detailed insights into accuracy, completeness, and safety. The findings support the use of LLMs in medical education and early clinical reasoning, while highlighting their role as clinician-supervised tools rather than replacements for clinical judgment. The results demonstrate the reliability of LLMs in organizing clinical information and identifying key diagnostic and management elements in standardized scenarios.

title: Correction: Age-specific ETCOc measured by non-dispersive infrared spectroscopy predicts neonatal phototherapy
Low prevalence of celiac disease in French children, a nationwide study
abstract: Background There are differences in prevalence and incidence across Europe without updated data for France. The aim of this study was to fill this gap obtaining epidemiological data of French children with celiac disease (CD). Methods We used the French Health Data System (SNDS) to identify Results 41690 children with CD were identified over 2011-2022. The male-to-female sex ratio was 0.88. In 2022, the national prevalence was 0.15% among children, ranging from 0.08% in the North-West to 0.25% in the South-East of France. The incidence rate ranged from 12.4 in 2020 to 17.4 per 100000 children in 2012, with a median age increasing from six in 2011 to seven in 2015. Comorbidities included thyroid disease (1.7%), and type 1 diabetes (9.7%). Conclusions The prevalence of pediatric CD is low in France, with differences across regions. However, the age at diagnosis and the female predominance are in agreement with recent studies. Impact This nationwide study revealed a lower prevalence of CD in French children than in other European countries, with regional variations. The study confirmed the female predominance and the age of seven at diagnosis. These data should be useful to give screening advices, looking for CD even in older children with atypical signs.

title: Primary preventive interventions to reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia in neonatal intensive care units: a meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Background To assess preventive strategies for ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in mechanically ventilated (MV) neonates. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched in June 2025. Eligible studies evaluated primary VAP-prevention interventions in neonates receiving MV. Outcomes included odds ratios (ORs), incidence rate ratios (IRRs), and incidence rate differences (IRDs). Results Thirty-four studies involving 6,301 neonates were included. Bundle-based quality-improvement packages were associated with lower VAP occurrence (OR = 0.40, 95% CI 0.28–0.57; I² = 37%). MV-adjusted analyses showed lower incidence (IRR = 0.56, 95% CI 0.43–0.73) and 8.33 fewer VAP cases per 1000 MV-days (IRD = –0.0083, 95% CI –0.0127 to –0.0039). Oral care was associated with lower VAP odds (OR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.35–0.81; I² = 3%). Evidence for other interventions was limited and heterogeneous. Conclusions Bundle-based quality-improvement packages were associated with lower neonatal VAP rates, although heterogeneous bundle composition and non-randomized designs limit causal interpretation. Oral care was also associated with lower VAP odds, but confidence in the magnitude of effect is limited by small-study effects, inconsistent subgroup findings, and variable diagnostic criteria. Impact This study provides the most comprehensive synthesis to date focused exclusively on VAP in ventilated neonates, incorporating ventilator-day–adjusted outcomes. By using robust meta-analytic methods across diverse study designs, it clarifies which interventions have consistent evidence and which remain uncertain. Bundle-based quality-improvement packages were associated with meaningful relative and absolute reductions in neonatal VAP. The findings support further evaluation and implementation of bundle-based quality-improvement strategies. Uncertainty regarding the magnitude of benefit from oral care and the need for higher-quality controlled studies.

title: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease
abstract: Abstract Background Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood. Methods This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD ( n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1–4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development. Results White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency ( p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive ( p = 0.001), language ( p < 0.001), and motor ( p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64–12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors. Conclusion In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population. Impact In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

title: Correction: Opportunities for antenatal medical treatment of genetic conditions: the earlier, the better
abstract: The article ‘Opportunities for antenatal medical treatment of genetic conditions: the earlier, the better’, written by Diana W. Bianchi, was originally published open access under ‘This is a U.S. Government work and not under copyright protection in the US; foreign copyright protection may apply 2026’. As a result of the author’s/authors' subsequent decision not to publish this article under the open access model, the copyright notice of the article was changed on 27th of August 2026 to © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to the International Pediatric Research Foundation, Inc 2026 with all rights reserved.

title: Collaborative role of muscle ultrasonography and subjective global-nutritional assessment in pediatric end-stage renal disease
abstract: Abstract Background Nutritional well-being in childhood chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a multidisciplinary problem. Nevertheless, reliable nutritional status assessment considering underlying pathogenesis remains challenging. So, we aimed to assess the collaborative role of quadriceps muscle ultrasonography and subjective global nutritional assessment (SGNA) in evaluating childhood end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis (ESRD-HD). Methods Sixty-eight children with ESRD-HD were enrolled in addition to 68 age- and sex-matched healthy controls.
